#!/bin/bash
#flux: --job-name=PANDA
#flux: --mail-type=ALL
#flux: --mail-user=jwhitlock@uab.edu
#flux: --nodes=1
#flux: --ntasks=1
#flux: --mem-per-node=255G
#flux: --time=12:00:00
#flux: --array=0-49
#flux: --output=PANDA_%J.out
#flux: --error=PANDA_%J.err
# The Slurm partition directive '--partition=largemem' has no direct Flux equivalent.
# This is typically handled by resource constraints on the target system. You may
# need to add a '--constraint' option if the system uses node features to define partitions.
# The Slurm directive '--mem-per-cpu=255000' (255GB) was translated to '--mem-per-node=255G'
# as the job requests a single task on a single node.
# The Slurm output/error format '%x_%A_%a' (jobname_arrayID_taskID) has been translated to
# 'PANDA_%J' (jobname_jobID). Flux does not support per-task array index variables
# in the output/error filename patterns.

########################################
### PUT YOUR COMMANDS BELOW THIS BOX ###
########################################

#load modules
module load Singularity/3.5.2-GCC-5.4.0-2.26

#variables
wd="/data/user/jbarham3/230227_JW_Setbp1Manuscript"
src="/data/user/jbarham3/230227_JW_Setbp1Manuscript/src/network_scripts/PANDA" #be sure that your subdirectories are structured the same

export SINGULARITYENV_PASSWORD='pass'
export SINGULARITYENV_USER='jbarham3'

#code to execute docker and script for analysis
cd ${wd}

#array file of cell type specific expression inputs for PANDA
SAMPLE_LIST="${wd}/results/array_inputs/Setbp1_PANDA_files_array.txt" #note: make sure path and file name are correct
SAMPLE_ARRAY=(`cat ${SAMPLE_LIST}`) # parantheses instruct bash to create a shell array of strings from SAMPLE_LIST

# The Slurm environment variable $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID has been replaced with the Flux equivalent, $FLUX_ARRAY_TASK_ID.
INPUT=`echo ${SAMPLE_ARRAY[$FLUX_ARRAY_TASK_ID]}` #extracts a single input from the array and prints (using echo) it into INPUT variable, each single input is then assigned an array number by $FLUX_ARRAY_TASK_ID

# NOTE user must have already pulled from docker and built .sif file with singularity below (jordanwhitlock/setbp1_manuscript_panda_1.0.1)
singularity exec --cleanenv --containall -B ${wd} ${wd}/bin/PANDA_docker/setbp1_manuscript_panda_1.0.1_latest.sif Rscript --vanilla ${src}/02_PANDA.R ${INPUT} # here vanilla ensures only the script is run and environment is kept clean

issues: The script uses a job array (`--array=0-49`) but specifies single output and error files (`--output=PANDA_%J.out`, `--error=PANDA_%J.err`). This will cause all 50 tasks in the array to write to the same files concurrently. This can lead to jumbled, interleaved, and overwritten output, making logging and debugging extremely difficult. It is highly recommended to handle file output within the script to create unique log files for each task, using the `$FLUX_ARRAY_TASK_ID` variable. For example, by appending `> ${wd}/log.${FLUX_ARRAY_TASK_ID}.out 2> ${wd}/log.${FLUX_ARRAY_TASK_ID}.err` to the `singularity exec` command line.

This creates a high probability that the application will be terminated by the Out-Of-Memory (OOM) killer, causing the job to fail.
